title: ia init authors a `@workspace`, its participant `@agent` and that `@mandate`, then reports capture and project apart; the local system and its distribution move behind --system
summary: Breaking: ia init writes a different starter and reports more. Without --system it authors exactly three records in .ia/src/workspace.ia, at placement authored and with only the fields their schemas declare: `@workspace <name>` (composition.systems naming every system the bundled base installs, composition.sources `".ia/src @authored"`, composition.steward the participant), the participant `@agent <name>` ("The IDE agent operating in the <name> workspace, any vendor.", governance.applies []) and `@mandate <name>-mandate` (governance.requires "Claim no host permission or execution from this mandate.", authority.participant the agent, authority.moves Observation, Verification, Synthesis, Delegation and Execution, authority.scope the workspace). Record names are the workspace name, never prefixed with the package id. It writes no local `@system` and no `@distribution`, so .ia/release.json names no distribution, and it writes .ia/.gitignore holding work/ and distributions/ only where none exists; an existing one is left as it is and reported, never a conflict. ia init --system (new) also writes .ia/src/systems/<name>/system.ia (the 1.x local `@system <name>` and its `@agent <name>-steward`) and .ia/src/systems/<name>/records/distribution.ia (`@distribution <name>-distribution` whose distribution.records is `[@system <name>]`), and the descriptor names that distribution, so ia pack releases the system folder. The apply runs install, author (create-only), admission (zero error findings, each starter record compiled at its path) and descriptor, the completion point, then two effects reported apart: capture, the ia capture write of .ia/work/snapshot/current.json, so a workspace has a snapshot from init on, and, only with --host, project, the ia host <host> --apply path, whose projection applyHostProjection writes. An effect after the descriptor that fails or is interrupted leaves every earlier result in place and says so: a capture that fails is refused as ia capture refuses it, with its code, location and repair, then ia capture --root <root>. With --host the project effect still runs after a capture that failed, because the packet reads the live revision rather than the capture, and that refusal then says the projection is written; an interruption before the capture, or a host step that refuses, names ia host <host> --root <root> --apply (or ia host's own remedy, rooted) and says whether the capture was taken. An interruption before the descriptor names the rerun of ia init, which skips completed steps. With --json the plan steps are install, author, admission, descriptor, capture and, with --host, project (1.x: install, system, records, descriptor); plan.owns adds .ia/.gitignore and .ia/work/snapshot/ and lists the system folder only with --system; plan.starter adds system, records (each `@<word> <name>`) and ignore ({path, status}, create or present), and its descriptor omits distribution without --system; applied.distribution is null without --system, and applied adds authored (the starter identities in file order, three or six), ignore (written or present) and effects {capture: {revision, records}, project: {host, files, receipt} or "skipped"}, files being the receipt's files with their SHA-256 and receipt its path. The human report lists the authored identities, the ignore file, the capture and the projected files and receipt, or says project was skipped. ia pack refuses a release descriptor, as @inventarch/db decodes it, that names no distribution as IA-CLI-CONFLICT (exit 3), located at the descriptor, before the packer reads anything else, naming ia vocabulary distribution; a file that is no release descriptor is left to the packer's own refusal. @inventarch/cli/internal/init: StepId is install, author, admission, descriptor, capture, project; Step.path became paths; Starter adds system and records, InitView adds present and ignore, Applied adds authored, ignore and effects and its distribution may be null, Descriptor.distribution is optional; starterRecords returns the three records; starterDescriptor without a distribution argument omits the key (1.x: null); ApplyOptions adds project, the --host effect applyInit runs after the capture, and Projected is new; ownedPaths takes --system; new: starterDistribution, starterFiles, StarterRecord, CaptureEffect, ProjectEffect, WORKSPACE_PATH, IGNORE_PATH and IGNORE_TEXT; LEFTOVER also matches distribution.ia and .gitignore. @inventarch/db: decodeReleaseDescriptor accepts a descriptor without distribution and ReleaseDescriptor.distribution is optional; a present one must still be a native distribution identity, never null; BundleManifest still requires it, and its decoded keys and canonical bytes are unchanged. @inventarch/distribution: packing a descriptor that names no distribution refuses as IA-DIST-CLOSURE-INVALID. @inventarch/authoring-system: validateDraft and formatDraft (validate-ia, format-ia, and ia format through them) also take a .ia file of the repository's own .ia/src outside every system folder and outside .ia/src/floor/, both compared case-folded where the volume folds case, under a root an admitted `@workspace` declares at the authored placement, such as .ia/src/workspace.ia or this repository's .ia/src/participant.ia; every other target, a file that is not .ia, a path outside every such root and floor, installed and adopted files included, is still refused as IA-EXEC-OUTPUT-UNSAFE, now with a message naming both kinds of target. Limits: a workspace an earlier ia init made is not changed (ia init --migrate does not exist yet), the steward guard stays retired, and installed state stays unknown; workspace revisions of unchanged sources, the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2, every ia scope form, body(K) and ia.position-body.v1 are unchanged.
